name: Button
summary: Starts an action: send a form, confirm a choice or go to the next step. All variants come from one base component (_Button). Change spacing, radius or typography there, and all 60 variants follow.
use: For actions that do something on the current page or in the system.
Choose Hierarchy by importance, and Size by space and density.
avoid: Going to another page: use a link (<a>). Hierarchy=Link is a button that looks like a link, not a real link.
Actions you cannot undo, like delete: use Button destructive.
On/off settings that stay on: use Toggle.
anatomy: Container: background, border and focus ring.
Leading icon (optional): before the label. The spinner replaces it when Loading.
Trailing icon (optional): after the label, for example an arrow for "next".
figmaProps: Pick a Lucide icon. The color follows the label.
reactProps: Shows a spinner, sets aria-busy and blocks the button.
Takes the full width of the container.
behaviour: Hover: the color moves one step. Link gets an underline.
Focus: a visible focus ring with keyboard navigation (:focus-visible).
Disabled: lower contrast colors, no hover, cursor not-allowed.
Loading: the spinner replaces the leading icon and the label stays. You cannot click the button for a moment.
a11y: Native <button> that works with Enter and Space. No div with onClick.
Native disabled takes the button out of the tab order. If the button must keep focus so you can explain why it does not work, use aria-disabled="true" and block the action yourself.
Loading sets aria-busy="true". Announce the result (success or failure) with a Toast or Alert in a live region.
Icons next to a label are decorative: aria-hidden.
Contrast of label and background meets WCAG 1.4.3 in Light and Dark.
content: Three words at most. Sentence case, no full stop.
do: One Primary per view or per dialog. Supporting actions get Secondary or Tertiary.
Use Loading for actions with a noticeable delay, like a network request.
Put a visible explanation near a disabled button.
dont: Several Primary buttons next to each other.
Use Size to show importance. That is what Hierarchy is for.
open: Loading now uses native disabled, so the button loses focus. Think about aria-disabled during Loading, so focus stays.
